synopsis: The University of Pretoria independently verifies mining collision-avoidance systems under South Africa’s MOSH regime, progressing from laboratory TRL4 testing to representative-mine trials, with the protocol extending underground [f15570, f14690, f6372]. Results reported in October 2025 covered 189 tests—79% verification and 21% development—with pass rates of 62% for detection devices, 42% for machine-side systems and 83% for third-party interfaces; throughput was 1.6 tests per week with an 18-week lead time [f15647, f5179, f5180]. Verification must separately cover machine types, models and serial numbers with different braking characteristics, while published stopping tests cover only unloaded machines on gradients of 1% or less, limiting the demonstrated operating envelope [f5181, f5182]. Hexagon announced on 25 March 2026 that its current-generation Vehicle Intervention System had passed Pretoria’s TRL4 verification before integrated site testing, but the press release supplied no numbers and capability-building and verification durations were not found [f1350, f6373, f1846]. Pretoria’s 2024 research investigated steering-rate-based collision prediction to reduce false interventions, but its initial results were simulation-only and validation time once available was not found [f6331, f1851]. This research addresses production losses, wear and resistance to adoption from false interventions, exposing a tension between conservative, fail-to-safe intervention and operational acceptability [f5567, f5781].
